title: Overview
text:
HYDRA-EO is a European Space Agency project that develops an operational framework to detect, quantify, and differentiate abiotic and biotic crop stress. The project targets priority plant pathogens, including Flavescence Dorée in grapevine, Potato Virus Y in potato, and fungal diseases such as Septoria, while also assessing stress interactions under variable water and environmental conditions.
HYDRA-EO integrates physically based radiative transfer modelling approaches with machine learning algorithms to identify the spectral and spatial resolutions required to capture biotic stress signals effectively. By combining hyperspectral, thermal, and multi-sensor Earth Observation data from field, airborne, and satellite platforms, the project delivers early and reliable indicators to support agricultural resilience and evidence-based decision-making across Europe.

title: Overview
section: Understanding crop stress across spectral and spatial scales
text:
Understanding crop stress across spectral and spatial scales
HYDRA-EO develops an operational framework to detect, quantify, and differentiate abiotic and biotic crop stress across multiple spatial and spectral scales. The project focuses on priority plant pathogens, including Flavescence Dorée in grapevine, Potato Virus Y in potato, and fungal diseases such as Septoria, while also assessing interactions between disease pressure, water stress, and environmental variability.
By integrating physically based radiative transfer modelling approaches with machine learning algorithms, HYDRA-EO identifies the spectral and spatial resolutions required to robustly capture biotic stress signals. The combination of hyperspectral, thermal, and multi-sensor Earth Observation data from field, airborne, and satellite platforms enables the delivery of early and reliable indicators to support agricultural resilience and evidence-based decision-making across Europe.





Phenotyping potato site





UAV / airborne


UAV & airborne processing
Radiometric and geometric correction of UAV and airborne hyperspectral and thermal data, including mosaicking, BRDF normalisation, and co-registration with field plots. Output products include surface reflectance cubes, temperature maps, and quality masks.




Satellite EO processing


Satellite EO processing
Sentinel-2, PRISMA, and EnMAP workflows (e.g. Sen2Cor atmospheric correction, spectral resampling, tiling, and time-series aggregation), harmonised across sites for crop–stressor analysis and EO upscaling.




RTM library & hybrid ML


Hybrid ML methods
PROSAIL and SCOPE forward simulations via ToolsRTM and SCOPEinR, LUT generation, plant trait retrieval, and hybrid machine learning models trained on combined RTM–EO features for crop stress detection.

title: Tools
text:
Software used in HYDRA-EO tutorials
This page summarises the main R packages and tools used in the tutorials, with links to their Git repositories and simple usage examples.




R · ToolsRTM


Canopy & leaf RTMs
The ToolsRTM package provides a unified suite of radiative transfer models for simulating leaf, canopy, and soil reflectance across multiple sensor resolutions. It integrates PROSPECT, FLUSPECT, Liberty, INFORM, fourSAIL, and PROSAIL for detailed optical simulations, as well as advanced modelling components such as SPART and MARMIT for soil reflectance.
These capabilities support flexible, physics-based workflows for Earth Observation data analysis and model–data integration.
ToolsRTM package




R · SCOPEinR


Energy balance & SIF
The SCOPEinR package implements the SCOPE model for simulating soil–canopy radiative transfer, photosynthesis, fluorescence, and surface energy balance. It provides tools and an R interface for producing consistent reflectance,radiance and fluoresence emission, and photosynthesis products under varying stress, physiological, canopy properties and illumination conditions.
This package supports detailed modelling of vegetation functioning in crop studies and stress analysis.

title: Consortium
text:
Partners & roles
HYDRA-EO is coordinated by Wageningen University and brings together complementary expertise in Earth Observation services, radiative transfer modelling, plant pathology, genetics, and agronomy from the Netherlands, Italy, and Spain. The consortium covers the full chain from field experimentation to EO-based modelling, hybrid machine learning, and dissemination.



Coordination · NL


Wageningen University & Research (WU-DES)
The Geoinformation Science and Remote Sensing (GRS) group leads overall project coordination and Work Packages WP1, WP2, WP5, WP6, and WP10. WU-DES develops the RTM and ML core (ToolsRTM, SCOPEinR), designs the scientific workflow, and manages the central Git repositories and Shiny-based tools.
Project coordination is led by Dr. Carlos Luis Camino González, with scientific support from Prof. Dr. Lammert Kooistra and colleagues.




Difussion


Wageningen Environmental Research (WENR)
WENR leads WP8 (Scientific Collaboration) and WP9 (Promotion & Dissemination), and co-leads WP6. The team specialises in operational EO services, evapotranspiration, and agricultural applications, and is responsible for stakeholder engagement, outreach activities, and links with ESA platforms and services.




Modelling · IT


Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche – Institute of BioEconomy (CNR-IBE)
CNR-IBE leads WP3 (Development & Validation), WP4 (Experimental Dataset Generation), and WP7 (Scientific Roadmap). The group coordinates Italian alfalfa and vineyard campaigns, hyperspectral validation and scaling studies, and contributes to trait retrieval modelling and the long-term scientific roadmap supporting future ESA missions.




Field trials · ES


Chaparrillo Agro-Environmental Research Center (CIAG-IRIAF)
CIAG-IRIAF co-leads WP2 and is responsible for pistachio and olive trials in WP4. The centre provides experimental orchards with controlled inoculation of fungal and bacterial pathogens, conducts UAV and aircraft-borne campaigns, and integrates agronomic, spectral, and genetic data to support stress disaggregation and crop resilience studies.

title: Contact
text:
Contact & contributions
If you would like to contribute examples, report issues, or reuse the tutorials for teaching, please contact the HYDRA-EO team or open an issue in the relevant repositories.




Coordination


Project lead
Dr. Carlos Camino (Wageningen University) is responsible for the overall scientific coordination of the HYDRA-EO project. His role includes leading the development of the methodological framework, coordinating the integration of radiative transfer modelling and hybrid machine learning approaches, and overseeing the design and maintenance of tutorial materials and open-source tools.
He acts as the main interface with ESA and consortium partners, ensuring scientific coherence, timely delivery of project outputs, and alignment with project objectives.

This section summarises the HYDRA-EO work packages (WPs), outlining their scope, role, and position within the overall project timeline. Each work package contributes a specific set of activities—ranging from scientific requirements and data collection to modelling, integration, and dissemination—together forming a coherent end-to-end workflow.




WP1


Scientific requirement consolidation
Definition of scientific objectives, use cases, trait–stressor matrix, and alignment with ESA requirements and parallel EU initiatives.




WP2


Dataset collection
Field campaigns, UAV and airborne acquisitions, in-situ measurements, and harmonised dataset documentation across crops and sites.




WP3


Model development & validation
Development and validation of RTMs and EO-based models, including spectral sensitivity and sensor intercomparison.




WP4


Experimental dataset generation
Generation of experimental EO products, synthetic datasets, and stress-specific simulation libraries.




WP5


Earth system science exploitation
Analysis of functional traits, stress dynamics, and scaling from UAV to satellite EO products.




WP6


Societal relevance & transfer
Demonstration of applicability for agriculture, disease monitoring, and resilience, including stakeholder-oriented outputs.




WP7


Scientific roadmap
Identification of knowledge gaps and recommendations for future EO missions (CHIME, FLEX, LSTM).




WP8


Scientific collaboration
Coordination with ESA activities and relevant Horizon Europe projects.




WP9


Promotion & dissemination
Scientific communication, training material, workshops, and outreach activities.




WP10


Project management
Overall coordination, reporting, risk management, and contractual compliance.

title: News
text:
Upcoming conferences & dissemination activities
The HYDRA-EO project is presented and discussed at selected scientific meetings and mission-oriented workshops. These venues are used to share methodological advances, prototype tools, and reproducible examples related to hybrid RTM–ML approaches, imaging spectroscopy, and EO-based crop stress detection.



ESA Digital Twin Earth Components – Open Science Meeting 2026
2–5 February 2026 · ESA-ESRIN, Frascati, Italy
ESA open science meeting dedicated to Digital Twin Earth components, mission-oriented methods, Cal/Val readiness, and multi-sensor integration for Earth Observation workflows.
FLEX-Fluorescence 2026 Workshop
3–6 March 2026 · Bonn, Germany
International ESA workshop focused on the latest developments in fluorescence remote sensing, including updates on the Fluorescence Explorer (FLEX) – Sentinel-3 tandem mission.
14th EARSeL Workshop on Imaging Spectroscopy
2–4 June 2026 · Helsinki, Finland
International scientific workshop on imaging spectroscopy, covering methods, sensors, applications, and reproducible workflows across environmental and agricultural monitoring.
